title: Tarka Dal
description: Red lentils simmered with turmeric until they fall apart, then woken up with a sizzling pan of cumin, mustard seeds, garlic and chilli poured over at the last moment.

items.prep: rinsed until the water runs clear

steps.text: Put the rinsed lentils in a large saucepan with the water and turmeric. Bring to the boil, skim off the foam that rises, then turn the heat down to a steady simmer.
Simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then, until the lentils have completely broken down. Add the tomatoes and salt for the final 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Give it a hard whisk at the end for a smooth, creamy dal. Loosen with a splash of boiling water if it is thicker than you like.

steps.text: While the lentils finish, heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin and mustard seeds and let them sizzle until the mustard seeds start to pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the onion and fry, stirring often, until deep golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chillies and fry for 2 minutes until the garlic is pale gold. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the chilli powder and garam masala.
steps.tip: Ground spices scorch in seconds, which is why they go in off the heat.

steps.text: Tip most of the tarka, oil and all, into the lentils and stir it through. Squeeze in the lemon juice, taste and add more salt if needed.
Spoon into bowls and top with the remaining tarka and the coriander. Serve with rice or flatbreads.

tips: Dal thickens a lot as it sits. Always loosen leftovers with water when reheating.
Slitting the chillies rather than chopping them gives fragrance with gentle heat. Chop them if you want it fiery.

substitutions.note: traditional, but no longer vegan or dairy-free

storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Reheat gently with a splash of water until piping hot.
author: Simmer
